correctness.rationale: For independent Brownian walkers the dimensionless no-reset survival is erf(t^(−1/2))^N, so the k-th raw moment is 2k times the stated u-integral, which is finite exactly for N>2k. Under the common independent exponential clock it is a reset before completion that renews the whole ensemble. Laplace-transforming this renewal equation gives F(q+s)/(1−qF(q+s)); the denominator at s=0 is strictly positive since there is positive probability of completing before reset. Differentiation in s gives the mean and second moment and their variance quotient in RESULT.md. Dominated differentiation at q=0 uses only three baseline moments, including for N=7. In particular C=−2F′/F²−1, so the cancellation leaves C′(0)=G_N/m₁³. A strict right derivative fixes the difference from the zero-rate value for sufficiently small q>0, not global monotonicity. Independently ran `python /workspace/reproductions/check_reset_intervals.py`: Machin's π identity and alternating series bound 2/√π; integer-directed Horner evaluation brackets erf using truncations at indices 109 and 110; exact rational cell weights with directed sums use monotonicity. The first cell uses erf(u)≤(2/√π)u, and the upper tail uses erfc(4)≤exp(−16)/(4√π)<2e−8, proved with a lower Taylor bound on exp(16). Rational arithmetic confirms every strict sign for N=7,…,12. For the tight G_11 case an outward bracket is [−0.001981,−0.001197]. The frozen script's 75-digit Decimal arithmetic does not literally direct every final rounding outward; the independent certificate closes that gap for the signs and supports the displayed rounded brackets. No signs are inferred for other N or finite rates outside a local neighborhood.
